items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: Hawkins, you know, he comes around later and he says, 'How come you didn't put a chorus in there for me?

ctx.x: She sang it beautifully. The verse and the chorus and then he had her do it again and do it again and he was a very understanding man, musician, music-wise anyway and he knew what arrangers -- you know, we got to get the idea. Of course, he wanted you to orchestrate pretty much what he had on the piano, the way he did it. So this was fine. So I took it home and week or so, whenever he wanted it, I had it done. He played it over and she sang -- I thought, 'Oh, God, he doesn't like it. I hope I did the right…

Fletcher liked it, and Hawkins, you know, he comes around later and he says, 'How come you didn't put a chorus in there for me? I wish I had.' Imagine, a real slow ballad -- well, anyway, that was good.

I had to get Whiteman's permission to do that which I got while he was out on the coast. And so you know, I figured it's another connection. It was good, nice experience and it was nice to work with somebody that likes your work. That sort of thing. Ideal conditions.
